expectations.text: States plainly that the not-empty check is insufficient
expectations.evidence: No. That test would have been green for all 21 days. The table was never empty. It was full of plausible zeros.

expectations.text: Identifies the COALESCE to zero as the mechanism that made the failure silent
expectations.evidence: COALESCE(revenue, 0) makes 'no matching row' and 'genuinely zero revenue' the same value.

expectations.text: Recommends reconciliation against a source of truth, not only shape checks
expectations.evidence: Daily reconciliation: warehouse total vs. source-of-truth total—the only check that catches a logic error the data still looks fine after

expectations.text: Recommends that assertions run before publication rather than after, so bad data cannot reach the dashboard
expectations.evidence: build to staging, test staging, promote on pass. A suite that runs after publication...still lets bad numbers reach finance.

expectations.text: Recommends a data contract or schema check so an upstream rename fails loudly and attributably
expectations.evidence: Contract check on upstream schema at ingest; quarantine to a dead-letter table, don't drop

expectations.text: Recommends volume or null-rate assertions rather than only a non-empty check
expectations.evidence: Assert join match rate against a floor between load and publish, promote only on pass

expectations.text: Treats three weeks of nobody noticing as a detection gap worth its own fix
expectations.evidence: Finance's close *was* your reconciliation job. It runs monthly, with three weeks of lag, executed by a human.

expectations.text: Explains why a silently wrong number is more dangerous than a failed pipeline
expectations.evidence: returns a plausible number instead of failing...silently took on semantic load—describes the contrast but does not explain the consequences or why failure would be preferable
